objections.problem: Finger 2 must cross over 3 from C#5 to D5; R6 also breaks the 5-2 alternation of R2 and R4.

Bar 4 repeats the 2-1 shuffle; G#3-D4 fits one five-finger position, reached by a single shift after the dotted E4.
Thumb lands on Eb4 and C#4 although 3 and 2 cover them inside the natural hand position.

objections.problem: Same Eb+G dyad leading to G# is 1+2 then 3 at R1-R3 and R21-R23, but 1+3 then 4 here; unify.

objections.problem: Finger 5 hops F5-D5-C5 in the top voice; 5-4-3 over the thumb keeps that line legato.

it-1c9e.comment: Bar 3 is neatly fingered with 2 anchored on Bb4 and a legato 5-4-3 top line; only the chain of 1+5 dyads in bar 4 needs changing. The left-hand thumb under 3 on A3 is fine as a descending continuation.

objections.problem: Fingers 2 and 3 cannot span the octave G#4-G#5.
Thumb assigned to both Eb4 and Bb4 at once; they are a fifth apart.
With 4 holding Eb5, finger 3 on Bb4 spans a fourth and the thumb on Eb4 a 1-4 octave; take Eb5 with 5.

it-10f7.comment: Two outright impossibilities and an overstretched hold in bar 6. With 1+5 on the octave, Eb5 on 5 (moving F5-Eb5 at the barline) and 1+3 on both Eb4+Bb4 dyads the passage lies well.

objections.problem: Fingers 3 and 2 cannot span the sixth C3-A3; the same dyad is 5+1 just before and after.
Finger 3 assigned to both A2 and E3 simultaneously.

it-7bd4.comment: Two impossible dyads; the rest is sensible. With 5+1 on every C3+A3 and 3+1 on A2+E3 it is ready for print.

objections.problem: Finger 4 repeats from F5 to E5 at sixteenth speed; the descending run takes 4-3-2-1.
Finger 3 assigned to both G#4 and B4 simultaneously.

objections.problem: Finger 3 crosses over 4 from Bb4 to C5, then must hop from C5 down to G4 for the next chord.

Eb4+G4 followed by G#4 is fingered 1+3, 4 here but 1+2, 3 at R1-R3 and R21-R23.

it-7ea5.comment: The reversed 5-4-3 at R11-R13 is the critical fault; the 3-over-4 at R5 is a lesser one. At R19 the thumb has to leave the held Bb4 early, which the pedal covers.

objections.problem: Finger 3 plays G#5 then jumps down a fourth to Eb5 on the next eighth; legato is lost.
Same chord as L5-L7 but fingered 4+3+2, stretching 2-3 over a fourth for no reason.

it-c507.comment: The 3-2-1 changes on the repeated Eb5 are good. The left-hand chords should use the 4-2-1 shape throughout.

objections.problem: Finger 5 plays D5 then C5 in consecutive sixteenths.

F4-G4-F4-Eb4 fingered 3-2-3-2 makes 2 cross over 3 and back at sixteenth speed; cannot be played evenly.

it-624c.comment: Bar 29 is fine. With the three fixes the sequential neighbour-note groups of bar 30 share one shape (4-5-4-3, 2-3-2-1, 3-4-3-2).

objections.problem: D5 on finger 3 is a dotted eighth still sounding when Eb5 enters on finger 3; the D5 cannot be held.

it-a80f.comment: Otherwise a sound two-voice fingering, with bars 8 and 9 sequenced alike. The finger-2 moves into the chords at R14 and R29 are acceptable voice-leading compromises.

objections.problem: Repeats the figure fingered 2-4-3-5 at R13-R16 and R21-R24; 2-3-2-4 adds a small shift unless the next bar needs finger 5.

it-9281.comment: Standard, well-sequenced fingering with clean crossings over the thumb at each descent.

objections.problem: Ornament D5-C#5-D5 alternates thumb and 2 with 2 below the thumb, crossing back and forth at 32nd speed.
G4 on 3 then F#4 on 4 forces 4 over 3 inside a fast ornament, then back to 3; not playable at tempo.
Finger 2 plays E5 then leaps a fourth to A5 on the very next note.
Thumb lands on C#5 although finger 2 serves equally well and still reaches G5 with 5.

it-3611.comment: Both hands stay in five-finger positions and shift only at rests or long notes; ready to print.

objections.problem: Octave chord on 4+3+2 needs a fourth between 3-4 and a fifth between 2-3; beyond a medium hand.
Finger 5 is assigned to both Eb3 and G#3 in one chord; impossible.

it-8800.comment: Otherwise correct: thumb on the repeated C4 and 5+3+1 on the repeated octave chord. Two chords break the pattern and must be restored.

it-74db.comment: Playable as written, but the repeated G3 belongs on 5 so the upper voice E-D-C-B can be fingered 1-2-3-4, which also makes bars 13 and 15 identical.

it-8da9.comment: The right hand is sound apart from the thumb on F#4 in bar 20. The left-hand octaves in bar 21 contain two impossible fingerings and must be 5+1.

it-53e6.comment: The bar 5 ornaments sit in one position with G5 on 5, and the shift down to C5 is taken after the quarter-note G5. Ready to print.

objections.problem: Thumb is given both E4 and C5, a minor sixth apart.
E4+Bb4+E5 on 2+3+4: fingers 2-4 cannot span the octave; the same chord at R33-35 uses 1+2+5.

it-73c9.comment: The rest of the double-note fingering works, and keeping 2 on the repeated Bb4 through bar 16 is good. The two impossible chords must be fixed before printing.

it-4234.comment: Held notes are respected throughout, and bar 13 repeats bar 12's fingering for the sequence. The thumbs on black keys are forced by the chromatic lines.

it-5ddd.comment: Each step of the sequence shifts by crossing 2 over the thumb and reuses the same 2-4-3-5 and 4-3-2-1 shapes. Clean and consistent.

objections.problem: Thumb tucked onto E5 then 4 on F5 squeezes 1-4 onto a semitone; after 3 on F5, 2-3 finishes the turn naturally.

it-fc79.comment: In bars 5-6 the thumb tucks under 2 into a 1-2-3-5 chord shape, consistently, with the shifts at the rests. Only the end of the turn in bar 7 needs an edit.

A4+C5 on 1+2 and C5+E5 on 2+5 here, but 1+3 and 3+5 later in the bar; 2-5 on a third is cramped.

it-4d02.comment: The left hand is standard: a 5-4-2-1 chord, a 5-3-1 triad and a 5-3-2-1 descending arpeggio. From beat 4 of bar 4 the right hand reads best entirely in the A4-E5 five-finger position.

objections.problem: 5 on D3 then 5 on C3 shifts the hand; 4, 2+1 on D3, F3+B3 (as in bar 23) keeps bar 22 in one position.

it-c8d1.comment: Standard bass-and-dyad fingering with firm 2+1 repeated dyads under the right-hand ornament; usable as is.

it-a6fe.comment: Well planned: G4 on 4 is held over the turn so 2-3-2-1-2 fits underneath in one position, and F4+A4 on 1+2 sets up Bb4 on 3 and D5 on 5 without a shift.

objections.problem: Finger 2 still holds G#3 (dotted half) when it must strike A3; bar 23 correctly takes G#3 with 3.

it-5b7a.comment: Bar 23 shows the right grip (5+3 under the held fifth, then 2 and 1 for A3 and B3); bar 21 must match it. Everything else is compact and consistent.

objections.problem: 5 and 4 span a fourth on F3-Bb3, wider than 4-5 allows; 5+3+1 then 4+2 keeps F3 held and the voices legato.

it-fe39.comment: The right hand is idiomatic (descending A-F-C-A arpeggio on 5-4-2-1, 4 over the thumb onto Bb4 to land in C position). The left-hand chord in bar 17 needs 5+3+1 so the inner voices can step down on 4 and 2 over the held F3.

it-342f.comment: A consistent 5-4-5 octave scheme in every bar, with 4 on Bb and Eb and a natural 4-to-5 connection on the descending step; sound for octaves at this tempo.

objections.problem: Rising E5-F5-G5 fingered 5-4-3 after G5 on 4: each step crosses a long finger over another; impossible at sixteenth speed.
E5 on 3 rising to F5 on 2 makes finger 2 cross over 3, a long-finger crossing.

it-2b4e.comment: Bar 15 and the whole left hand are clean and stay in one position per figure. The right hand of bar 16 is fingered backwards; it should mirror bar 15 as 2-3-4-5-3-4-2-3.

it-3a1b.comment: Bar 1 sits in one five-finger position, with the held A3 and E4 framing the inner notes. The 5+1 to 4+2 move into A-C# leads the voices smoothly, and the shift falls on the rest.

objections.problem: G4 held by 3 while 2 takes C4 a fifth below (2-3 beyond a fourth), then the thumb reaches Bb3 a sixth below.
Bar 13 repeats bar 12's figure a step higher; R4-R6 use 2-3-4 but here 3-4-5. Keep 2-3-4.

it-2c12.comment: The thumb-held lower voice is handled sensibly, but G4 on 3 cannot be held against C4 on 2; with G4 on 5 the cadence lies naturally. Bar 13 should copy bar 12's fingering.

it-5947.comment: Each bar stays in one position, the ornaments use matching neighbour fingers (4-3-4, 3-2-3), and the only shift comes after the long G5. Fine for a student.

it-22f6.comment: Standard shapes throughout: 1-2-4-5 for the four-note chords and 1-2-5 for the fifth-plus-octave chords. Taking F#4 with 4 frees thumb and 2 for the beat-3 dyad under it.

objections.problem: Finger 2 plays Bb4 and then E4 in the next dyad with no rest; 3 over the thumb on Bb4 avoids the hop.

it-431a.comment: Clean in both hands; the left-hand triads use the standard 5-2-1 and 5-3-1 and the right-hand arpeggio lies well. Only the Bb4 needs a touch.

5-3-2 on E3-G#3-C#4 puts 3-2 on a full fourth; the standard 5-3-1 matches the D-F#-B chords just before.

it-e774.comment: Right-hand octaves and filled octaves are standard and consistent. In the left hand the two identical E-G#-D-E chords in bar 8 should both be 5-4-2-1; L22-25 as written cannot be held.

objections.problem: Finger 5 strikes C#5 on beat 4 while still holding E5, which sounds until beat 4.25.
Eb5 (4) and E5 (3) sound above C#5 held by 5, out of pitch order; E5 on 3 then spans a seventh to F#4.

Thumb slides E4 to Eb4 under C#5 held by 4, a 1-4 seventh. Hold C#5 with 5 and take E4 with 2.

it-2bd1.comment: Plain 5+1 octaves, the standard 5-4-2-1 for the seventh chord, and G2+B2 on 3+1 keeps the thumb on B2 for the last chord. Ready to print.

objections.problem: Repeated G#3 and D4 change from 3+1 to 4+2 between consecutive eighth chords; a needless shift. D4 can stay on 2 throughout.

objections.problem: Parallel thirds A3-C4 to G3-B3 on 2+1 twice hop both fingers; 3+1 then 4+2 connects both voices.

it-6eb2.comment: This is a sound and economical LH. The broken-chord figure stays in one position, 4 on G3 sets up the move to the C4+G4 chord, and the chords change position only across rests.

objections.problem: Finger 3 holds the dotted-quarter E5 (R3) yet must also strike B4 (R6) beneath it.
With 3 holding E5, finger 2 must reach G#4 and A4 below (a sixth and a fifth) and 1-3 a seventh.

it-4c13.comment: From beat 3 of bar 7 the sequence is well fingered: 4-5 on every semitone approach and the thumb on the lower voice. objections.problem: B4 on 4 sounds beneath Eb5 still held by 3: fingers out of pitch order, a 4-under-3 crossing.
Finger 3 must strike C5 while still holding the dotted-eighth Eb5.
While C5 sustains on 3, finger 4 must reach F5: a fourth between 3 and 4.
F4 and G#4 sound together on finger 2; the identical figure in bar 8 (R14-15) uses 2+4.

it-b7e2.comment: Bar 8, beats 1.5 to 2.5, tangles fingers 3 and 4 under a held Eb5, and the closing dyad puts two notes on finger 2. With B4 on 1, C5 on 2 and G#4 on 4, the passage matches its own well-fingered sequence from beat 3.

objections.problem: Identical chord C4-Eb4-G#4 on consecutive beats is fingered 3+2+1, then 4+2+1; C4 changes finger for no reason.

it-4058.comment: The RH descending arpeggio keeps the thumb on the white C5, and alternating 2-3 on the repeated Eb5 is fine. In the LH, the two identical chords in bar 24 should be fingered alike.

it-0335.comment: This is textbook Alberti-bass fingering. The whole passage stays in the five-finger position C4-G4, and the repeated figures are fingered identically.

objections.problem: Octave F#2-F#3 is fingered 5+5; one finger cannot play both notes.
Octave E2-E3 on 3+2: fingers 2 and 3 cannot span an octave.

it-7c0a.comment: Most octaves are correctly 5+1, but two are impossible as marked. The closing short chords are well grouped: 5 on Eb2, 3 on G2 and the thumb on B2 form one hand position.

objections.problem: With 5 holding F5, finger 4 on C#5 forces a 4-5 major third twice; 3 spans it easily.

it-b90c.comment: The thumb pedal on G#4 with 5 on the leaping top notes is the only option for these spans; the G#4-Bb5 ninth is a stretch in the writing itself. Finger 4 on the held Eb5, moving to 5 on F5, keeps the melody legato.

objections.problem: 1-2 stretched a minor sixth A4-F5, then the thumb jumps to D5; 1-2-3-5 covers A4-A5 in one position.
On beat 3, G3 (bar 19) and F3 (bar 20) take 5, unlike 4 on beat 2, so 5 must leap a third.

it-8ede.comment: Sound outline with the LH thumb anchored on the upper pedal note; the RH broken chord in bar 20 walks the hand needlessly and the LH beat-3 figure should keep 4 as on beat 2.

objections.problem: Thumb shuttles between G4 and A4 three times at sixteenth speed; G4-A4-B4-C5 fits one 1-2-3-4 position.
Bar 21 repeats bar 20's figure a third higher but abandons its 1-3-2-4 / 3-4-2-3 fingering.

it-ad6d.comment: Bar 20 sits neatly in one five-finger position; bar 21 should simply transpose that pattern instead of shuffling the thumb. LH octaves on 5+1 are standard.

objections.problem: 4 on E5 crosses over 3, then 2 on G5 crosses back over 4; R5 and R6 are swapped versus the 2-4-3-5 sequence.
Finger 3 plays G4 then B4 consecutively at sixteenth speed; the figure F#4-A4-G4-B4 takes 2-4-3-5 like its predecessors.

it-9fd4.comment: An otherwise clean sequential fingering (2-4-3-5 then 4-3-2-1) spoiled by two slips: the swapped fingers at R5-R6 create a tangle of long-finger crossings, and R32 hops on 3.

objections.problem: Rising A4-C5-F5 fingered 4-3-2: each long finger crosses over the last; bar 6's 2-1-2-3-5 shape fits here.
Finger 5 plays G5 then F5 back to back inside the grace-note ornament; reuse 3 on F5 as at R13.
Thumb on E5 then 4 on the adjacent F5 cramps the hand; 2-3 stays in the position already held.

it-a694.comment: Bar 6 shows the right idea for these rising arpeggios; bar 5 needs the same 2-1-2-3-5 instead of a reversed 4-3-2, and the bar-7 ornament should avoid the 5-5 hop.

objections.problem: Thumb passes under 4 onto black F#5 at fast sixteenths, forcing extra crossings; 4-3-2-1 descends in one position.
1-4 spans the octave C#4-C#5; a medium hand should take the octave with 1-5.
3-4 on F#4-B4 spans a fourth, beyond the third allowed; this first-inversion chord takes 1-2-4-5.
1-4 spans the octave F#3-F#4; put 5 on the top note.
Finger 2 is assigned to both C#4 and G#4 in the same chord.

it-0b03.comment: The chord fingerings break hard rules (3-4 on a fourth, two notes on finger 2) and twice ask for 1-4 octaves; the opening descent needlessly puts the thumb on F#5. Rework before printing.

it-b4f0.comment: Sensible walking fingering for a contrapuntal line: the rising fourths take 4-1 consistently and the bar-4 sequence is fingered 3-2-4-1 both times, with no crossings or hops.

it-64f2.comment: Both hands stay in five-finger positions that match the figures; the only shifts fall at the octave leaps, the rest and the long notes.

objections.problem: 2-3 on C#5-G5 spans a diminished fifth, beyond the fourth allowed; the same chord takes 1-3-5 at R11-R13.
Thumb is re-used on Bb5 while still holding the half-note C#5; 4 reaches Bb5 and matches R17.

it-e877.comment: The thumb cannot hold C#5 and take Bb5 at once, and the bar-12 chord should use 1-3-5 like its repetitions; the rest is reasonable.

it-58a8.comment: Sound, economical left hand: the move to the E3-C#3-A2 arpeggio comes on the leap, and the thumb hops in the rising thirds of bar 9 are inherent and harmless at this slow tempo.

objections.problem: Pinky on F4 straight after 4 on A3 forces a needless jump of the hand; 5 on A3, thumb on F4 stays in place.
Finger 4 repeated on E3 then F3 in sixteenths; 3 on F3 stays in position and matches L7-L8.

it-fb96.comment: The sixteenth-note figures in the D3 and C3 positions are well fingered apart from the 4-4 hop at L10-L11; the opening jump onto 5 on F4 should be smoothed.

it-9d9d.comment: Bass-and-chord shapes sit naturally under the hand, the thumb stays off the black keys, and bars 21 and 23 are fingered identically.

objections.problem: Within the G3-D4 broken chord, finger 4 belongs on A3; 3 there cramps the 5 on G3 that follows.
Fingers 3 and 2 cannot hold the minor sixth B3-G4; use 5+1 like the C4+G4 dyad in bar 5.
Finger 4 is assigned to both G3 and B3 of the same dyad.

it-af36.comment: Two impossible dyads (3+2 on a sixth, 4+4 on a third) must be fixed before printing; the broken-chord bar is otherwise fine.

objections.problem: Thumb must jump from D5 to B4 in the lower voice; 2 on D5 lets the thumb pass under legato.

it-3dca.comment: Careful two-voice fingering, and the sequence in bar 9 beats 3-4 repeats bar 8 exactly; the fifth on C#5 and Bb4 is justified by the spread.

objections.problem: Crossing 2 over the thumb for a semitone, then switching to the thumb on the repeated G#4, is fussy; 2 then 1 is simpler.
Thumb hops A4 to B4 in the rising thirds; 1+3, 2+4, 3+5 keeps them legato and matches R8-R9.
Thumb tucks under 4 by a fourth, A3 to E3, at eighth speed; the descending A-minor arpeggio fits one octave position.

it-939a.comment: Playable, and the repeated LH chords are fine; the LH arpeggio in bar 5 and the RH thirds should use the standard fingerings.

objections.problem: Fingers 3 and 2 cannot span the sixth G3-E4; bar 15 correctly uses 5+1 for the same dyad.
Finger 5 is assigned to both G3 and D4 of the same dyad.

it-0256.comment: Bars 13 and 15 are the same figure; 5+1, 5+1, 5+2, 5+3 in both removes the impossible span and the double 5.

it-c84a.comment: Clean chorale fingering: thumb and fifth stay on white keys, and the hops in the RH sixths of bar 4 are inherent and harmless at this tempo.

objections.problem: Starting the D3-G3 run on 5 forces a one-step shift at E3; landing on 4 keeps one C-position through L21.

it-3955.comment: Clean five-finger groupings, with the hand moving only where the music leaps anyway; the cadential 5-5 bass leap is natural. Only a small economy preference in bar 20.

objections.problem: Finger 5 assigned to both C#3 and G#3 of the opening fifth.
3 on B3 must cross over 2 holding A3, then uncross for A3; long finger over long finger at fast tempo.
Finger 2 plays A3 then B3 consecutively; the thumb is free for B3, as in bar 21.

it-6f23.comment: Bars 21 and 23 are identical and should both read 5+3, 2, 1; bar 22 needs the thumb on B3 to avoid the crossing.

objections.problem: Major sixth E4-C#5 on fingers 3 and 2; 2-3 reaches at most a fourth.
Finger 4 assigned to both A3 and D4 of the chord.
2 on A2 crosses over 3 on C#3 descending, then 5 must leap above it to E3; finish the arpeggio on 5.

it-1eca.comment: Two impossible spots (the 3+2 sixth and the 4+4 chord) and a crossing in the bar-8 descent; the bar-9 thirds over the held E3 are well fingered.

objections.problem: A octave takes 4+1 here but 5+1 at L19-20 and L23-24; white-key octaves on 5+1 throughout read more simply.

it-dd80.comment: Textbook five-finger groupings in the right hand, sequenced identically in both bars with the shift on the downbeat; black-key octaves on 4+1 are standard.

objections.problem: Finger 4 assigned to both Bb3 and D4 of the third.
The repeated Bb3+D4 third is fingered 3+1, 4+4 and 4+2; keep Bb3 on 4 throughout, as at L5.
4+3+2 packs D3-F3-Bb3 onto weak, maximally stretched fingers; the standard left-hand shape 5-3-1 sits comfortably.

it-a684.comment: Every chord follows a rest, so the hand is free to reposition; the problems are the shifting fingering of the repeated Bb3+D4 third, one impossible chord and a cramped final triad.

objections.problem: Finger 4 plays G5 then F5 back to back in a stepwise descent; 4-3-2-1 is the natural fingering.
Finger 2 assigned to both E4 and G4 of the chord.
Octave Bb2-Bb3 on fingers 3 and 2; 2-3 reaches at most a fourth.

it-12e1.comment: The ornamental right-hand figures (first-inversion F arpeggio on 5-4-2-1, chromatic 3-1-2) are well chosen, but two impossible spots and a hop must be fixed before printing.

it-da2f.comment: Economical waltz fingering: in bar 24 bass and chord share one hand position, the 4-2-1 chords keep 5 off the black chord tones, and the repeated Eb5 rotates 3-2-1 idiomatically.

objections.problem: 2 on B3 lands left of 3 on D#4 at sixteenth speed, forcing 2 over 3; 5 on B3 keeps the position.

it-af7a.comment: Sound overall, with sensible thumb placements on the upper notes of the subject, but B3 in bar 3 and the closing C#4 in bar 4 need new fingers.

objections.problem: Finger 5 plays G5 then C6 back to back at sixteenth speed, a hop; bar 5's 2-1-2-3-5 shape fits this figure too.
Turn F5-G5-F5-E5-F5 on 4-5-4-3-4 leans on the weak 4-5 pair; 3-4-3-2-3 is more even for a student.

it-cb00.comment: Sensible arpeggio fingering in bar 5; bar 6 should copy its thumb-under shape to avoid the 5-5 hop onto C6.

objections.problem: E5+A5+E6 on 2+3+4 puts a fifth between 3 and 4 and an octave on 2-4; impossible.
Finger 5 is assigned to both E3 and G#3 in the same chord.
C#5+C#6 moving to the B octave is 1+5 here but 1+4 in the identical move at R19-20 and R26-27.

it-9e40.comment: Two physically impossible chords (RH 2+3+4 across an octave, LH 5+5) must be fixed before printing; the rest is standard octave and chord fingering.

objections.problem: Bb4 on 3 then D5 on 2 forces 2 over 3 in a 32nd-note arpeggio; take Bb4-D5 with 2-3.
Thumb passes under 2 onto Eb5 inside a 32nd-note turn, then crosses back; 3 on Eb5 keeps the turn in position.
Thumb moves from E4 to F4 across the barline; 2-3 on F4-A4 keeps the resolution connected.

it-5064.comment: LH is fine. RH has an illegal 2-over-3 crossing in the opening arpeggio and a needless thumb pass onto Eb5 in the turn; keep C5-D5-Eb5 under 1-2-3.

objections.problem: Thumb jumps from B4 to G#4 at sixteenth speed and lands on a black key; 2 over the thumb connects the inner voice.
Thumb hops F#4 to E4 under D5 held by 4, a 1-4 seventh; D5 on 5 and F#4 on 2 avoid both.
Thumb hops E4 to Eb4 under C#5 held by 4, again a 1-4 seventh; C5-C#5 on 4-5 and E4 on 2 avoid both.

it-fd8f.comment: Bar 7 is well handled with 2 crossing over the thumb under the held E5; in bar 8 the inner voice relies on thumb hops under 1-4 sevenths, which taking the held upper notes with 5 resolves.

objections.problem: G#3-C#4 is a fourth held between 3 and 2 on two black keys, cramped; 4-2-1 matches the shape used at L5-7.

it-c7e9.comment: Clean waltz accompaniment; only the last chord uses a cramped 3-2-1 where 4-2-1 sits naturally.

objections.problem: C2 and C3 are both on finger 5 in one octave; the thumb must take C3.
Octave Bb1-Bb2 on 3-2 is impossible (2-3 reaches a fourth); use 4+1 as at L3-4 in the same figure.

it-5c02.comment: Two impossible octaves (5+5 on C, 3+2 on Bb); bar 15 should simply repeat bar 13's corrected 5+1, 4+1, 5+1.

it-08c2.comment: Standard bass-and-dyad accompaniment; the F3-E3 step on 3-4 keeps the lower line legato and A3-G#3 on 1-2 needs no crossing.

objections.problem: With 5-3-1, LH 2 hovers between G#3 and Eb4, right where the RH thumb plays C4; 5-2-1 clears that space.

it-b1d5.comment: Simple and consistent; the only consideration is the hand overlap around C4-Eb4, which 5-2-1 in the LH eases.

objections.problem: G4 is a dotted half held by 3 while the turn needs 3 for F4; one finger cannot hold and strike.
A4 on 4 then Bb4 on 3 crosses 3 over 4, and is crossed outright if A4 is held as notated.

it-bfdf.comment: Bars 5-7 use sound positions and sensible thumb shifts. The G4 held over the turn needs 4, and the bar 9 dyad should be 1+2 so that Bb4-D5 continues on 3-5.

objections.problem: Bb4 and C5 sound together on finger 2; the same dyad is 2+3 everywhere else.
F4-D5 is a sixth on fingers 2-3, far beyond the fourth that 2-3 can span.

it-887b.comment: The LH is fine throughout. The RH needs two corrections, after which the chordal fingering is natural.

objections.problem: Ascending G4-G#4-Bb4 on 5-4-3 while the thumb holds C#4 forces 4 over 5 and 3 over 4.
The thumb still holds dotted-eighth Bb4 when Eb4 needs it, and G4 on 2 lies below the held thumb.
Bar 13 beats 1-2 repeat bar 12 a tone higher; A4-Bb4-C5 should take 3-4-5 like the corrected G4-G#4-Bb4.
G3 and G4 are struck together on the thumb; an octave needs 1 and 5.

it-6504.comment: Bar 12 beats 3-4 are well fingered, but the reversed run, the opening of bar 13 and the closing octave must be redone; bar 13 should mirror bar 12's fingering for the sequence.

objections.problem: A3-E4 frames a five-finger position; 3+1 forces the thumb from E4 onto D4 while E4 sounds, then 2 over it.

it-1ede.comment: Bars 2-3 are well judged, with the leap to G#4+D5 placed at the rest. Bar 1 should simply sit in the A-E five-finger position.

objections.problem: Thumb sits on black Bb3 then hops to A3; 2+4 moving to 1+5 connects both voices.
Repeated A5s and F5s change fingers 2-3-4 and 2-1-2 for no gain; the F5-C6 five-finger position covers the phrase.

it-71c9.comment: Playable as written. The high phrase is far simpler in one five-finger position, with one finger per repeated note.

it-e605.comment: Compact and economical: the thumb anchors A3 and then E3 while 5 takes the bass. Nothing to change.

it-2439.comment: The repeated thumb on C4 and the 5-3-1 octave chord are the natural choices. The thumbs interlock around C4-Eb4, but that comes from the hand split, not the fingering.

objections.problem: Against the E4 thumb, 3 on G3 spans a sixth and 4 on F3 a major seventh; use 4 and 5 as in beat 1.
Same stretch in the sequence: against the D4 thumb, 3 on F3 and 4 on E3 overreach; use 4 and 5.

it-9504.comment: The RH and the bar-to-bar sequence are sound. The LH pedal figure only needs 4 and 5 kept on the lower notes to avoid needless stretches.

objections.problem: 5 on the held G4 forces 3 to cross above it for G#4 and 5 to re-take C5; R6-7 rightly uses 1+2.
Finger 2 hops F4 to G4 and the thumb A4 to Bb4 in the chromatic climb; 3-4-5 over the held D4+F4 avoids both.
1+3 then 1+2 on D5+F5, Eb5+G5 makes the thumb hop and 2 land past 3; 2+4 keeps the thirds legato.

it-dc08.comment: The opening 2+5 is the real fault and contradicts the sound 1+2 used for the same figure at beat 3; the chromatic climb into bar 3 and the thirds at its end also need tidying.

objections.problem: Thumb hops A4 to B4 between thirds; A4 to E5 fits one hand position as 1+3, 2+4, 3+5 with no hops.

it-a795.comment: Sound overall: the 4-3-2-1 descent and 3 over the thumb into G#4+B4 are standard. The thirds in bar 15 sit best in a single A-E five-finger position.

objections.problem: Rising G4 to Bb4 with 3 then 2 makes 2 cross over 3, a long-finger crossing; thumb on G4 avoids it.
A3+F4 spans a minor sixth, beyond the fourth that 2-3 can hold; 2+5 also links E4 4 to F4 5.
Finger 3 plays G5 then F5 back to back; 2 on F5 continues the 4-3-2 descent used in bar 12.

it-1d35.comment: The 2+3 on the minor sixth A3+F4 cannot be held; the 3-2 ascent in bar 11 and the 3-3 hop into bar 14 need fixing as well.

it-b1fa.comment: Clean, idiomatic invention fingering; the 3-2 on the last broken third sets up the G position for bar 30, and 3 over the thumb to F4 is well placed.

objections.problem: Thumb on the first D5 makes 3 cross over it for C#5 inside a fast ornament; 4-3-4-3 is the natural shape.

it-4d17.comment: Good apart from the thumb on the first D5 of the ornament; the 1-4 reach from G4 to E5 is wide but keeps the line legato.

it-f18c.comment: Standard 5-3-1 broken-chord shapes and legato 3+1 to 4+2 thirds; the position changes fall on chord changes and rests.

objections.problem: 1-4 octaves on C#4-C#5 and F#3-F#4 leave a medium hand no slack; 1-5 octaves are easier, at the cost of top-voice legato.

it-1313.comment: Thoughtful fingering: 3 over the thumb to F#4 leaves room for B3+D4 underneath, and the top voice stays connected. Only the 1-4 octave stretches are hard for a medium hand.

it-90f1.comment: Careful legato choices (E5 5 to Eb5 4, Bb4 2 to C5 3, matching 1+4 to 2+5 pairs, uniform 1+2+5 octave chords); thumbs on black keys and wide reaches are inherent in this texture.

objections.problem: The same Bb3+D4 third is taken 3+1, then 4+2 one beat later, a needless change of hand position.

it-e3bf.comment: Sound overall, and the 4-2-1 on the Eb chord nicely prepares 5 on D3. Start with 4+2 so the repeated Bb3+D4 thirds and the Bb3+F4 fifth share one position.

it-066c.comment: Standard 5+1 octaves throughout, which is right for this detached, fast bass line. The tempo is demanding, but the fingering itself needs no change.

objections.problem: Finger 3 is assigned to both C5 and E5 of the final third; one finger cannot sound two keys a third apart.
Finger 2 plays E3 then C3 in consecutive eighths of the descending arpeggio; 1-2-4-5 keeps the hand in one octave position.
The thumb takes the repeated G#4 half note on a black key where finger 2 can simply repeat it.

it-1b6d.comment: The closing 3+3 third is impossible and the bass arpeggio hops on finger 2. With C5+E5 on 3+5 the last thirds sit in a clean A-to-E five-finger position; the repeated left-hand chords are fine.

it-82b9.comment: Well planned: the thumb on E4 makes the ninth leap to D3 manageable, and each figure settles into a five-finger position. The closing 5-to-5 leap from G2 to C2 is the normal cadential jump.

objections.problem: Finger 3 on G4 then 2 on F4 crosses two long fingers and stretches 4-3 to a fourth; the thumb belongs on G4.
Finger 3 plays E4 then G4 in consecutive eighths, breaking the Alberti pattern that elsewhere returns to the thumb on G4.

it-f278.comment: Bar 1 is the textbook 5-1-3-1 Alberti fingering. Bar 2 should keep the thumb on every G4: 4-1-2-1, then 5-1-3-1.

objections.problem: While 4 holds Eb5, finger 3 on Bb4 must span a fourth between 3 and 4, beyond a medium hand; take Bb4 with 2.

it-5074.comment: Bar 5 is sensible given the wide spans; the G#4-Bb5 ninth is a stretch inherent in the music, and F5 on 5 gives a legato step to Eb5 on 4. In bar 6 the inner Bb4 must go on 2 while 4 holds Eb5.

it-dd17.comment: Consistent and comfortable at this slow tempo; keeping 2 on the common-tone Bb4 through the octaves is economical. Advanced players might alternate 4 and 5 on black-key octave tops for legato, but that is not needed here.

objections.problem: The thumb moves from the held E4 to F4 on the downbeat; taking E4 with 2 lets the thumb pass under for a legato step.
Finger 4 on F3 against the thumb on Eb4 spans a minor seventh; finger 5 reaches it without strain.

it-8c64.comment: An idiomatic mazurka bass and a neat right-hand figure in bar 23. Two small edits improve the legato and the comfort of the left hand.

objections.problem: Finger 2 on D4 then again on F4 around the thumb forces needless repositioning; 4 on D4 keeps the 4-2-1 hand frame.

it-eedb.comment: Sound Alberti fingering with the thumb anchored on G4; only the D4 in bar 2 breaks the hand frame. The standard 5-1-3-1 would also serve.

objections.problem: F#3 and G#3 sound together but both are given finger 3.
Fingers 4 and 3 asked to hold G#3 to C#4, a fourth; 3-4 cannot span more than a third.

it-c3b0.comment: The bass notes on 5 are fine for a waltz leap; two chords must be refingered (3-2-1 and 5-2-1) before print.

it-706b.comment: Chord shapes stay in one position and the held C#5 under 4-5 lies within an octave; the thumb on black keys is unavoidable in these chords.

objections.problem: Thumb on C5 then 5 on B4 needs a quick hand jump; 2+4 with 4 over the thumb would connect more smoothly.

it-1447.comment: The E-G#-B shape on 1-3-5 lets the thumb take E4 neatly, and the thirds use the standard 24-35-13 pattern.

objections.problem: Thumb passes under 3 onto F#5 inside a 32nd-note turn, then 3 must cross back; plain 4-3 alternation works.
The same F#5-E5-F#5 turn is fingered 4-3-4 at R2-R4 but 4-3-1 at R6-R8.
C5-B4-C5 mordent fingered 3-5-4 crosses 5 under 3 and 4 over 5 at 32nd-note speed.
Ascending C5-D5 on 4 then 3 runs the fingers backwards; continue 3-4-5 on C5-D5-E5 instead.

it-b4eb.comment: Bar 5 is usable once R8 becomes 4; the bar 6 ornament needs a complete refingering as 3-2-3-4-5.

objections.problem: Bb3-F4 is a fifth between 3 and 1; 4 on Bb3 here is more relaxed and costs nothing over the rests.

it-d294.comment: Sensible throughout: the 5-3-2 triads keep the thumb off Bb3 and are fingered consistently.

objections.problem: Thumb must leave D4, still held as a dotted quarter, to play C#4; the suspension cannot resolve legato.
With E3 held on 3, A3-C#4 on 2-1 spreads 3-2 a fourth and 3-1 a sixth; hold E3 with 4.

it-0fef.comment: The 2-1 dyad accompaniment is reasonable at this slow tempo; two spots in bars 8-9 want a different finger.

objections.problem: Octave B1-B2 given to 5 and 4; 4-5 cannot span more than a third.
Octave A1-A2 given to 5 and 3, far beyond a medium hand; the repeat at L13-14 correctly uses 5-1.
Octave C2-C3 on 5-2 is a strained reach at quarter = 140; plain 5-1 octaves are standard and consistent.

it-ab73.comment: The octaves are fingered four different ways; take them all 5-1. The closing chords in bar 10 are fine.

objections.problem: Repeated F5 quarters fingered 2-1-2: needless finger changes at this tempo; keeping one finger is simpler.

it-a8ad.comment: Sound and practical: 5 on Bb4 with the thumb dropping to Bb3 frames the octave neatly, and the 1-2 / 1-3 dyads sit well. Only the finger changes on the repeated F5s are fussy.

it-9aa5.comment: Clean: one thumb shift onto E4 in bar 29, then the G-D five-finger position and a legal 3-over-thumb crossing to F4 carry the descending sequence.

objections.problem: Finger 2 still holds A4 (whole note) when it must strike D5, crossing over 3 on Bb4: impossible.
Thumb plays D4, E4 and F4 in succession: two hops in the inner voice under the held G4.

it-326a.comment: Bars 5-7 are well planned with a consistent sequence, but bars 8-9 need rework: the thumb plods D4-E4-F4 and finger 2 is asked to leave a held A4 for D5.

objections.problem: Thumb plays E4 then D4 in consecutive dyads in bars 13 and 15, a hop breaking the upper line's legato.

it-0de7.comment: Consistent across both bars and comfortable; over the G3 pedal on 5, letting the upper line close 1-2-3-4 keeps it legato without the thumb hop.

it-6152.comment: Well planned for the chromatic texture: 1-2-4 on the C#5 chord keeps the hand in one position and leaves 5 free for C6 over the held C#5.

objections.problem: Finger 3 assigned to both E3 and A3 of one dyad.
Octave A2-A3 fingered 3+2; fingers 3 and 2 cannot span an octave.

it-6aa9.comment: The bass-and-dyad pattern is otherwise sensibly fingered, but the dyad on one finger and the octave on 3+2 must be corrected before printing.

objections.problem: Ornament D5-C#5-D5 at 32nd speed fingered 1-2-1 makes finger 2 cross over the thumb and back; 4-3-4 stays in position.

it-922e.comment: Most of the passage sits well in the hand; the opening ornament should be played within the position (4-3-4-3-2-1) instead of with a thumb crossing.

objections.problem: Finger 5 assigned to both G#4 and D5 of one dyad; the neighbouring repeats use 5+1.
Octave D4-D5 fingered 3+2; fingers 3 and 2 cannot span an octave.
Finger 2 must reach C#4 below finger 3's D4 while 5 and 1 hold A3 and E4: a long-over-long crossing.

it-7247.comment: Not printable as is: a dyad on one finger, an octave on 3+2 and a 2-over-3 crossing under the held A3+E4 all need correcting.
